name: Brylcreem

card.summary: Brylcreem is a classic British water-and-mineral-oil hair cream that gives a neat, shiny, combed-back hold for slicked and quiffed men's styles.

quick.overview:
Brylcreem is a men's hair styling cream launched in 1928 in Birmingham, England. It is an emulsion of water and mineral oil that gives hair shine and a controlled hold, and its name blends 'brilliantine' and 'cream'.

The appearance payoff is a tidy, glossy, slicked-back or side-parted look in the style of mid-century barbering. It became a household name through the wartime 'Brylcreem boys' and later endorsements.
quick.how: A small amount is worked through damp or dry hair and combed into style. Users typically pair it with a comb for slick-backs, side parts and quiffs. The range now also includes gels and waxes in different holds and finishes.
quick.risks: It is a cosmetic product with the usual considerations of scalp or skin irritation for sensitive users. Heavier creams can leave hair looking greasy, which is the look some users want and others avoid.

lead: Brylcreem is a British men's hair cream first made in 1928 by County Chemicals at the Chemico Works in Birmingham. Wikipedia describes it as an emulsion of water and mineral oil stabilised with beeswax, known for a high shine; the name combines 'brilliantine' and 'cream' [1].

People use it to get a neat, glossy, combed style such as the slick-back, side part or quiff. Its image was built in the 1940s and 1950s, when Royal Air Force airmen were nicknamed the 'Brylcreem boys' and cricketer Denis Compton became one of Britain's first sportsmen to earn significant money from endorsements [1].

Ownership passed from Beecham to Sara Lee in 1993 and to Unilever in 2012, and today it is marketed by Combe in the US and Unilever in Europe, with Hindustan Unilever in India [1]. Grokipedia, an AI-generated source, adds that its popularity dipped in the 1960s with longer hair and revived later, including a 1997 David Beckham campaign [2]. On T Nation, one user simply said it is cheap and works for them [3].

chain: Cream coats and weights the hair
Hair holds a combed shape with shine
Neat, classic slick or quiffed style
angle.text: Brylcreem lets people hold a combed, glossy style for the day. It is associated with retro barbering looks like slick-backs and quiffs.

paras: Original Brylcreem is a white cream that gives a shiny, firm but flexible hold. Grokipedia lists a modern range of creams, gels and waxes in light to strong holds and matte or glossy finishes [2].

County Chemicals launched it in 1928 as a cream alternative to oil-based brilliantine [1]. Wikipedia notes wartime RAF personnel were called 'Brylcreem boys', citing a 1939 print ad featuring an airman as the likelier origin of the term [1]. Early TV advertising used a jingle [1]. Beecham owned it for decades, Sara Lee acquired the unit in 1993, and Unilever bought global rights in January 2012 [1].

It is referenced in The Sopranos and Mad Men, and a 1998 film, The Brylcreem Boys, concerns wartime internment [1]. In 1996 a British TV advert for Brylcreem shampoo was banned after complaints about strobe lighting [1].

timeline.event: County Chemicals launches Brylcreem in Birmingham [1].
Sara Lee acquires the brand's owner's personal care unit [1].
Sara Lee sells global rights to Unilever [1].
